gist: Blockworks 0xResearch analysts grade the first half of Citrini's crypto basket (Derive, Lighter, EtherFi, Aave, Ethena, Solana, Hyperliquid), broadly liking the themes but criticizing sizing and valuations, with Hyperliquid and EtherFi favored and Derive, Aave and Ethena seen as overweight or expensive.

insights.claim: Luke sees bullish consolidation within a higher-timeframe uptrend, stays in the four-year-cycle camp with a 1-3 year outlook asymmetric to the upside, and notes the Boros term structure is in contango, pricing rising yields into year-end maturities.
insights.speaker: Luke
insights.so_what: Contango on Boros is used as a rates-up signal supporting risk-on and onchain lending monetization.
insights.quote: one of my favorite indicators, the uh Boros term structure is still in contango

insights.claim: Shonda says recent pumping coins are low-quality, illiquid bottom charts, suggesting participants know no new capital is entering and are pumping them as final exit liquidity; she still thinks the market is closer to the bottom than the top.
insights.speaker: Shonda
insights.so_what: Low-quality small-cap pumps signal a late, capital-starved rotation rather than broad new inflow.

insights.claim: Kunal reports Blockworks D-Asia in Singapore had strong institutional attendance, hedge funds having done well this year, a consensus that the bottom is in, and tokenized assets as the top topic.
insights.speaker: Kunal
insights.so_what: Institutional sentiment is constructive and focused on tokenization; also a possible consensus-positioning warning.

insights.claim: Kunal hopes for a hot CPI print and a sell-off below 80K Bitcoin so he can buy coins he likes, while remaining long-term bullish; analysts at big firms reportedly have 8,000 S&P targets by year-end.
insights.speaker: Kunal
insights.so_what: Team is looking to buy dips below 80K BTC around the CPI print, not sell.

insights.claim: At the Singapore conference there was little consensus among lower-cap interests (AI, options, perps, stores of value), but one coin, Pearl, was discussed by roughly 90% of people; Shonda pitches it as AI Bitcoin, 'Pearl is to Zcash what Zcash was to BTC'.
insights.speaker: Shonda
insights.so_what: A single narrative coin dominating conference chatter is a crowding and sentiment indicator.

insights.claim: The Citrini report's basket is thematic and narrative-driven, with little discussion of multiples or revenue growth; Shonda notes positioning and story matter most for many capital allocators.
insights.speaker: Shonda
insights.so_what: Thematic baskets from respected sellside shops can drive flows regardless of valuation.

insights.claim: Luke views the Citrini basket as heavily overlapping with Blockworks favorites and with themes the team considers most important, and sees a famous sellside shop that nailed AI picks over four years buying crypto as a bull signal for institutions actually buying coins, not just using the tech.
insights.speaker: Luke
insights.so_what: Counters the bear narrative that institutions will use crypto tech but not buy tokens.

insights.claim: The basket is overweight perp exchanges: about 17% across Lighter and Hyperliquid (the leading perp DEXs), plus Ethena as tangential exposure to perp open interest and funding rates, which Luke wants to stay overweight.
insights.speaker: Luke
insights.so_what: Perp-theme exposure is concentrated in a few tokens; correlated risk if funding and OI roll over.

insights.claim: The team concludes the basket is a thematic portfolio focused on RWA/neo-bank/derivatives and omits pump.fun (Pump) and privacy and 'long degeneracy' exposure; Shonda says the best way to hold that barbell theme is Pump, noting Pump is among the highest-revenue crypto applications.
insights.speaker: Shonda
insights.so_what: Omitted memecoin and privacy exposure may be a gap or deliberate, saved for a part-two report.

insights.claim: Crypto became overweight perps versus options, and a reweighting toward options is underway; options offer put selling, risk reversals and no liquidation, which helps on volatile long-tail assets where traders got stopped out, as on a recent Pump move.
insights.speaker: Luke and Shonda
insights.so_what: Options volume growth is an early-stage structural shift; Derive is the current winner.

insights.claim: Derive at 10% is judged too high: with 30-day revenue slightly above half a million (about $6M annualized) it trades near 100x, the recent price run-up is largely driven by Upbit volume which has historically reversed, and a Hyperliquid options build would be bearish competition.
insights.speaker: Kunal
insights.so_what: Volume-driven Korean-exchange rallies tend to mean-revert; valuation leaves no margin for error.

insights.claim: Hyperliquid's Jeff said that if not building infrastructure he would build options, implying options on Hyperliquid are already possible but nobody has built them; media framed it as Hyperliquid building options and Derive fell on the news.
insights.speaker: Shonda
insights.so_what: Latent competitive risk for Derive from builders on Hyperliquid.

insights.claim: Shonda argues Lighter should not outweigh Hyperliquid because Hyperliquid has upside to stablecoins, spot, outcomes, possible options, native lending and priority fees, whereas Lighter is a narrow bet on Robin Hood and US regulation.
insights.speaker: Shonda
insights.so_what: Hype offers diversified optionality; Lighter is catalyst-dependent.

insights.claim: Kunal likes loading Lighter after its sell-off following an announcement that Robin Hood will run its perps via it, betting Robin Hood picks Lighter for crypto perps once US regulation clears, plus options coming and a cheaper multiple than Hyperliquid; Blockworks data shows heavy Lighter token dilution from vesting in October.
insights.speaker: Kunal
insights.so_what: Dip-buy with a regulatory and distribution catalyst, though token unlocks are a headwind.

insights.claim: EtherFi is seen as reasonably valued at about 15x 30-day revenue, with growth driven by the card product (weekly spend up and to the right) and a white-label stablecoin via Ethena; cashback was recently changed to ETHFI bought on the open market.
insights.speaker: Kunal and Shonda
insights.so_what: Cheapest multiple in the basket with real product-market fit.
insights.quote: I love EtherFi. It is one of my like favorite tokens to hold.

insights.claim: EtherFi's revenue looks flat because of shrinking LST revenue, masking card growth; as it shifts to a neo-bank its multiple remains below other neo-banks and could expand with revenue.
insights.speaker: Shonda and Kunal
insights.so_what: Revenue-mix shift from LST to card can drive both earnings growth and re-rating.

insights.claim: The host pushes back that neo-bank adoption may be mostly outside the US and G7, since many neo-bank stablecoins are not GENIUS or MiCA compliant; Kunal says EtherFi's card has users in nearly every country.
insights.speaker: Host
insights.so_what: Regulatory fit could limit neo-bank competition with Coinbase and incumbents in developed markets.

insights.claim: Luke is constructive on onchain lending metrics, preferring a basket of about three large-cap lenders rather than only Aave; Aave has around 55% of active loans, driven by BTC and ETH collateral, which benefits if majors rally and rates rise.
insights.speaker: Luke
insights.so_what: Lending revenue is levered to collateral prices, active loans and interest rates; contango on Boros supports rate upside.

insights.claim: RWA yield products like onyc and Figure Prime get 50-80% loan-to-deposit ratios as posted collateral, whereas tokenized equities have roughly half the aggregate ratio and little collateral use, so money markets benefit more from yield RWAs than tokenized equities; tokenized-equity exposure is better via AMMs like Uniswap, Raydium and Meteora.
insights.speaker: Luke
insights.so_what: Pick the venue by product type: yield RWAs to lenders, equities to DEXs.

insights.claim: Tokenized equity DEX volume largely comes from meme-stock pairs and arbitrage between issuers, sometimes from about 10 wallets trading within a second of each other, indicating little organic holder demand and so no base to lend against.
insights.speaker: Kunal
insights.so_what: Tokenized equity volume overstates real adoption; retail holders are the missing layer.

insights.claim: Aave at about 42x multiple faces Morpho eating share with aggressive distribution (e.g. Robin partnerships), so Kunal expects Aave revenue to make a lower high this cycle; the team would prefer equal weight Aave, Morpho, Kamino and Syrup.
insights.speaker: Kunal and Luke
insights.so_what: Competition has increased since last cycle; Aave's savings product is a watch item.

insights.claim: Bull case for Ethena: a pure risk-on beta via improved funding rates and basis, USDE TVL growth enabling potential buybacks, cleared supply overhang, and a frequent product cadence including Ethena Pay card.
insights.speaker: Kunal
insights.so_what: Ethena is the cleanest levered play on a rising basis trade.

insights.claim: Bear case: USDE grew on token incentives and Pendle/Aave looping at 20-30% yields, only about 20% of USDE is now deployed in the strategy, Hyena and whitelisted stablecoins did not grow much, and Ethena looks about five times pricier than EtherFi on an FDV basis despite less card traction.
insights.speaker: Shonda
insights.so_what: Ethena's premium rests on a forward-looking bull scenario rather than current metrics.
insights.quote: I'm going to be long etheri any day of the week.

insights.claim: USDE yield is slightly above 5%; Kunal says looping becomes attractive above about 8-9%, a scenario if Bitcoin pumps to 120-140K, while Luke notes SATs campaigns dumped ENA call options onto Pendle YTs, pushing up to 70% of USDE supply into those markets, and those premiums are unlikely without SATs.
insights.speaker: Kunal and Luke
insights.so_what: USDE supply growth depends on yield thresholds and incentives; funding rates have stayed low even in frothy periods.

insights.claim: Equity-backed basis expansion for Ethena, with Binance as a partner, will take a while to scale, so the thesis hinges on crypto basis trades staying profitable.
insights.speaker: Kunal
insights.so_what: Near-term Ethena growth rests on crypto basis rather than equities.

insights.claim: The team accepts an 8% Solana weight as market beta and the only pure L1 in the basket, but Kunal rejects it for the cited reasons: RWA volume is shifting among chains (Base, Robin Hood), x402 agentic payments are a tiny share of Solana transactions, and Solana's fees and volume largely come from Pump, so he would own Pump instead.
insights.speaker: Kunal
insights.so_what: Solana's narrative support is thinner than headlines suggest; Pump is a purer expression.

insights.claim: Hyperliquid is argued to be a narrow but expanding financial L1 that internalizes value across perps, spot, outcomes, borrow/lend and stablecoins, including about 90% of yield on platform assets, so Shonda would give it a 25% allocation (5% each across perp, HIP-4, borrow, stablecoins); Kunal suggests 15% as more balanced.
insights.speaker: Shonda
insights.so_what: Hype is consensus top holding; the debate is sizing and the FDV versus circulating supply multiple.

insights.claim: Hyperliquid's multiple has risen to historically elevated levels, but arguments say FDV overstates near-term supply, a recently unlocked team OTC allocation was rumored sold to a TradFi firm building a position, and TradFi is the marginal buyer from here.
insights.speaker: Kunal
insights.so_what: Marginal buyer shift to TradFi could sustain demand despite consensus positioning.
